case_scope.source_excerpt:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq 1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$, and a bounded measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$, write $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above. A periodic model uses the declared periodic cell and sums its periodic-image pair interactions with each unordered pair counted once. These are distinct boundary preparations. The limits on this page are positional configurational limits and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\{x\in\Lambda_k:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda_k)\leq s\}|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is an explicit condition on the boundary-layer volume; increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. For a locally finite exterior configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. Given $t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y),$$
interpreted as an extended-real sum. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The regular tail controls distant terms; the class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. $$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Use the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra on $\Lambda^N$. For $N\geq1$, let
$$D_{\Lambda,N}=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\Lambda^N:x_i\ne x_j\text{ whenever }i\ne j\},\qquad \mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}=D_{\Lambda,N}/S_N,$$
where the permutation group $S_N$ acts by relabelling coordinates. Give $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ the quotient sigma-algebra: $A\subseteq\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable exactly when its preimage under the quotient map $q_N:D_{\Lambda,N}\to\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable in the trace of the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra. Identify each orbit with its unordered simple configuration. For $N=0$, set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,0}=\{\varnothing\}$. If $\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}$ is product Lebesgue measure restricted to $D_{\Lambda,N}$, define the sector reference measure by
$$\mu_{\Lambda,N}=\frac1{N!}(q_N)_\#\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}\quad(N\geq1),\qquad \mu_{\Lambda,0}(\{\varnothing\})=1.$$
Equivalently, for every nonnegative measurable function $f$ on $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$,
$$\int f(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)=\frac1{N!}\int_{D_{\Lambda,N}}f(q_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N))\,d^{dN}x.$$
Collision diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero, so $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$; in particular, symmetric integrands may use the equivalent integral over all of $\Lambda^N$. Thus $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ is a finite measure, not generally a probability. Two labelled tuples represent the same state exactly when they are in one $S_N$ orbit. The factor $1/N!$ is an adopted indistinguishable-particle positional convention, not a theorem about classical trajectories or every classical description.

Let $\mathcal C_\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{N\geq0}\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ with the disjoint-union sigma-algebra, and regard each $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ as a measure on this union supported on its $N$-point sector. Define the unit-intensity finite-region Poisson reference by
$$Q_\Lambda=e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\mu_{\Lambda,N}.$$
Its total mass is one because $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$ and $e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N\geq0}|\Lambda|^N/N!=1$. This is a positional reference measure in the chosen dimensionless coordinates; it supplies no empirical claim about particle trajectories.

Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], fix $\beta>0$, and define $Z(L,N;\beta)$ as in that definition. For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$. On the interior of $\{\rho:F(\rho)>-\infty\}$, $F$ is finite and continuous. For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, its side length $L_n=2n+1$ and dimensionless volume $V_n=L_n^d$, the periodic positional energy $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the exact-$N$ measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. Given $N_n\in\mathbb N_0$, a reduced configuration-energy center $e\in\mathbb R$ joules per dimensionless reference volume, and a width $\delta_n>0$ in the same units, define
$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$
When $0<\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)<\infty$, the uniform positional shell law is
$$M_n(A)=\frac{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(A\cap S_n)}{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)}.$$
A shrinking energy-density shell uses some specified sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$. Its total energy width is $2\delta_nV_n$, which is $o(V_n)$ but need not be microscopic or bounded. Existence of a normalizing shell and the existence of a suitable shrinking sequence are separate theorem obligations. This is not a surface measure on an exact-energy hypersurface and not a phase-space shell for $K(p)+H_N^{\mathrm{per}}$.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and activity $z>0$. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. These are exactly the stable-plus-nonnegative-core conditions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for $\widehat\varphi$, after energy conversion; this is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D(P_0\|Q_0)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_0\ll Q_0$ and $h=dP_0/dQ_0$, then $D=\int h\log h\,dQ_0$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D=+\infty$. $$I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_L}\|Q_{\Lambda_L})}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.$$
For $\beta>0$, use the stationary laws with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to stationary laws assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]], an interior density $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and differentiability of $\beta\mapsto F_\beta(\rho)$ at $\beta>0$. Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. There exists a specified sequence $\delta_L\downarrow0$ such that the uniform positional shell law
$$Q_{\Lambda_L}\!\left(\,\cdot\ \middle|\ N=N_L,\ \left|H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d-e\right|\leq\delta_L\right)$$
is eventually defined, and its empirical field converges in probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. The energy width $2\delta_LL^d=o(L^d)$; no arbitrary prescribed width or zero-width surface measure is asserted.

Assume the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in $\tau_L$.

Assume the superstable regular model of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Let $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $C_{L,N_L}$ be the free-boundary positional canonical law with exactly $N_L$ particles, and let $R_{L,\omega}$ be its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. Choose any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$ and set
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
For every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$,
$$C_{L,N_L}\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\in U\}\longrightarrow1.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$. This is local observable equivalence for a uniformly sampled bulk location; it makes no claim about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin or about uniqueness for every interaction.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as in [[thm-tdmath-local-tame-entropy-compactness]]. Let $L\to\infty$ and let $C_L$ be probability laws on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, invariant under every translation modulo $L\mathbb Z^d$. Write $Q_L$ for unit-intensity Poisson measure and suppose
$$c_L=L^{-d}D(C_L\Vert Q_L),\qquad \sup_L c_L<\infty.$$
Let $\widetilde C_L$ be the law of the periodic continuation. Then $\widetilde C_L=E_{C_L}R_{L,\omega}$; these laws are stationary and are relatively sequentially compact in $\tau_L$ as $L\to\infty$. Their local counts are uniformly integrable. Along any convergent subsequence with limit $P$,
$$I(P)\leq\liminf_L c_L.$$
If the empirical fields $R_{L,\omega}$ converge in probability in $\tau_L$ to a fixed $P_*$, then $\widetilde C_L\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$, including expectations of every measurable local $f$ with $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ for bounded $A$. This concerns periodic continuation, not the zero extension of a configuration outside its fundamental cube.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\{x\in\Lambda_k:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda_k)\leq s\}|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is an explicit condition on the boundary-layer volume; increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. For a locally finite exterior configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. Given $t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y),$$
interpreted as an extended-real sum. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The regular tail controls distant terms; the class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.

Assume a superstable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the van Hove definition [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]. For a bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, define $\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)=\{(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ and $H_N(q)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)$. With $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, set
$$Z_\Lambda(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)}e^{-\beta H_N(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_\Lambda(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_\Lambda(N;\beta).$$
This is the labelled positional Lebesgue integral with indistinguishable-particle normalization and includes no exterior interaction. For $\Lambda=[0,L)^d$ it agrees with $Z(L,N;\beta)$ and $\Xi(L;z,\beta)$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For every van Hove sequence $(\Omega_k)$ and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure satisfies
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac1{|\Omega_k|}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)=p(z,\beta),$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube limit from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The extra superstability hypothesis supplies the uniform cell-occupation bound used below; no arbitrary-shape theorem under stability alone is claimed.

Assume superstability and regularity, let $(\Omega_k)$ be van Hove, and let $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ for an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Use the general-region free-wall convention of [[thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure]], namely
$$Z(\Lambda,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\{q\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}}\exp\!\left(-\beta\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)\right)dq_1\cdots dq_N\quad(N\geq1),$$
with $Z(\Lambda,0;\beta)=1$ and $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, for bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$. For the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional partition with this $1/N_k!$ normalization,
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.

Assume a stable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the genuine finite-valued positive-core condition of [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: for some $r_0>0$, a nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_0]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_0$ and $\int_0^{r_0}\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. For $t\geq0$ define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta\in\mathcal C_{\rm lf}:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\text{ for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$

$$H_{n,\zeta}(\omega)=H_{n,\mathrm{free}}(\omega)+\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{y\in\zeta_n^{\rm out}}\phi(q_i-y).$$
The exterior series has finite negative part by the proof below; its extended value may be $+\infty$, with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Define
$$Z_{n,\zeta}(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda_n)}e^{-\beta H_{n,\zeta}(\omega)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_{n,\zeta}(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{n,\zeta}(N;\beta).$$
For fixed $z,\beta>0$ and $t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure with this exterior pair energy satisfies
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\zeta\in\Omega(t)}\left|\frac1{V_n}\log\Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)-p(z,\beta)\right|=0,$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube pressure from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The exterior configuration is restricted to the stated fixed square-count class; no volume-filling external field is included. The conclusion is conditional on the genuine positive core and does not infer it from superstability alone.

Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq 1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$, and a bounded measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$, write $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above. A periodic model uses the declared periodic cell and sums its periodic-image pair interactions with each unordered pair counted once. These are distinct boundary preparations. The limits on this page are positional configurational limits and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

Adopt the unlabelled positional configuration measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ obtained from labelled tuples by dividing by permutation multiplicity. Thus, for every nonnegative measurable symmetric function $f$ on $\Lambda^N$,
$$\int f(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda^N}f(\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\})\,d^{dN}x.$$
The reference coordinates and length scale are those of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. This convention treats two labelled lists that differ only by a particle permutation as the same positional state. The factor $1/N!$ is an adopted indistinguishable-particle measure convention for this classical model, not a theorem that classical trajectories or every classical description must use quotient states.

For later comparison, define the unit-intensity Poisson reference on a finite region by
$$Q_\Lambda(d\omega)=e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega).$$
Its total mass is one because $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ has total mass $|\Lambda|^N/N!$ and $e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N\geq0}|\Lambda|^N/N!=1$. This is a positional reference measure in the chosen dimensionless coordinates; it supplies no empirical claim about particle trajectories.

For a specified finite region and boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and the positional energy in [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. For each fixed $N$, specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to the dimensionless positional configuration measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$; adopt the law
$$P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=Z_{\Lambda,N}^{-1}e^{-\beta H_N(\omega)}\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad Z_{\Lambda,N}=\int e^{-\beta H_N}\,d\mu_{\Lambda,N},$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}<\infty$. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^{N(\omega)}e^{-\beta H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)}$ relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures; its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. These are exactly the stable-plus-nonnegative-core conditions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for $\widehat\varphi$, after energy conversion; this is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. $$I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_L}\|Q_{\Lambda_L})}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.$$

citations.quote:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer and the physical number density corresponding to $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$ and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\{x\in\Lambda_k:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda_k)\leq s\}|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is an explicit condition on the boundary-layer volume; increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. For a locally finite exterior configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. Given $t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y),$$
interpreted as an extended-real sum. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The regular tail controls distant terms; the class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

Assume AC, as required by the current mathematical definition and its shape suppliers. Let $d\geq2$, $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable and superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ in the mathematical rates. Let $(\Lambda_k)$ be a van Hove sequence as in [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]. First, for free walls, the positional grand pressure along $\Lambda_k$ converges to the free-cube pressure of [[pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-pressure]]. For any positive interior attainable density $\rho$ and exact integers $N_k$ with $N_k/|\Lambda_k|\to\rho$, the exact-$N_k$ free-wall canonical log-partition rate converges to the same cube canonical rate. These two shape statements require superstability and regularity; stability alone is not asserted to suffice for arbitrary van Hove shapes.

Second, strengthen the potential hypothesis: for some $r_0>0$, $\widehat\varphi(x)\geq\widehat\chi(\|x\|_\infty)>0$ whenever $0<\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\widehat\chi$ is nonincreasing and $\int_0^{r_0}\widehat\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. For each fixed $t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n$ with exterior $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$ then converges uniformly in $\zeta$ to the same free-cube pressure. The exterior interaction is the deterministic positional term of [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]], not a volume-filling external field. This genuine divergent-core condition is the exact stronger hypothesis of the current exterior supplier; it is not inferred from superstability or replaced by a weaker source condition.

derivations.claim: Since $H_N=0$, the finite-volume canonical positional integral is $Z_{V,N}=V^N/N!$. Summing the adopted grand weights gives $\Xi_V=\sum_{N\geq0}(zV)^N/N!=e^{zV}$.

Adding $cN$ to the energy multiplies the $N$-particle weight by $e^{-\beta cN}$, so $\Xi_V^{(c)}=\sum_{N\geq0}(ze^{-\beta c}V)^N/N!=e^{ze^{-\beta c}V}$. For $c\neq0$ this has a different log-partition rate.

The perturbation is a potential on every point of $\Lambda$, whereas [F2] and [L1] restrict the boundary result to free walls or the interaction with one fixed uniformly tempered exterior configuration. Therefore this example lies outside those hypotheses and contradicts no qualified boundary conclusion.
